description: We are Astro Tech Sri Lanka, a passionate student team from Sri Lanka participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our focus is on space technology, microcontrollers, and hardware prototyping to build innovative solutions like a mini Arduino & ESP32 -based space hardware model for astronaut training and environmental monitoring. We are excited to build innovative solutions for space exploration!
summary: We developed an IoT-based Cube Satellite powered by an ESP32 microcontroller and equipped with five advanced sensors: DHT11, BME680, BMP280, and GUVAS-12SD. The satellite monitors real-time environmental conditions, including temperature, humidity, barometric pressure, altitude, and ultraviolet (UV) radiation levels. By integrating a BME680 gas sensor, it also assesses air quality to detect environmental pollution. Based on the calculated UV percentage and air pollution metrics, the system provides automated safety alerts—advising users whether it is safe to go outside. The hardware setup is independently powered using dual solar panels, a TP4056 charging module, LiPo batteries with a voltage booster, and communicates via a 433 MHz LoRa transceiver module for telemetry. This low-cost, multi-sensor CubeSat serves as an effective tool for localized atmospheric and environmental monitoring.
details: Using C++. It features dual solar panels, a TP4056 charging module, and dual 3.7v LiPo batteries with booster modules for power management. For environmental sensing, we integrated the BME680, BMP280, DHT11, and GUVA-S12SD sensors to monitor air quality, pressure, temperature, humidity, and UV radiation. Data is transmitted in real-time via a 433MHz LoRa Transceiver module. This Setup allows for low-cost, reliable, and localized environmental monitoring.
